messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue report describes the method CSVRecord.toMap() throwing a NullPointerException when called on CSVRecord instances created from CSVFormat configurations with no headers. According to the documentation, in such cases, toMap() should return null instead.

Examining the source code:

- The method CSVRecord.toMap() calls putIn() with a new HashMap to populate the map entries.
- putIn() iterates over the map 'mapping', which is a Map<String, Integer> mapping header names to their column indices.
- If 'mapping' is null (which can happen if no headers are defined), the call to mapping.entrySet() in putIn() will cause a NullPointerException.
- CSVRecord's constructor assigns the passed mapping to its private field 'mapping' without null checks.
- The CSVParser.initializeHeader() method returns null if there is no header information, which means that CSVRecord instances created from formats with no header receive a null mapping.
  
Thus, when toMap() is called on a CSVRecord from such a format, putIn() tries to iterate over null 'mapping', resulting in a NullPointerException. The observed failure in testToMapWithNoHeader confirms this behavior when parsing "a,b" with a CSVFormat with no headers.

The root cause is that CSVRecord.toMap() and putIn() do not account for the possibility that the internal mapping is null. Instead, according to documentation, toMap() should detect null mapping and return null directly to avoid NPE.

This explains the test failure and matches the bug report stating the NPE occurs on toMap() for no-header formats, where null should be returned instead.

Next, I will identify methods where to add this null check to fix the NPE.
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.toMap()
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.putIn(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.String>)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
